title: Deferred column hydration, density telemetry, and scrollbar attenuation for heavy virtual tables
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Extremely wide and deep tables (tens of thousands of rows, dozens of columns) are showing jank and high memory usage in the Console. Column-level widgets (filters, inline actions, rich previews) increase render cost and slow virtualization heuristics. Current approaches eagerly hydrate all visible column cells and UI affordances which spikes CPU and hurts smooth scrolling.

Goal: Design an approach that keeps the table responsive for heavy workloads by: 1) deferring non-essential column UI hydration until a stable idle window or user interaction; 2) introducing a lightweight density telemetry signal to tune default density presets and batch sizes; and 3) visually attenuating scrollbars/overlays to reduce perception of jitter while preserving accessibility and discoverability.

Scope: This ticket covers design artifacts, interaction specs, visual tokens, accessibility requirements, and acceptance criteria. Engineering implementation will coordinate with ENG for runtime flags and telemetry events. This is a design-maintenance initiative (not new feature), aimed to reduce CPU/memory at the component-level and improve perceived smoothness on mid-range devices.
acceptance_criteria: Spec for deferred column hydration: when columns contain >1 complex cell renderer, secondary column affordances (filter chips, inline menus, preview widgets) should mount only after 300–700ms of idle or on explicit user hover/click
Density telemetry signal defined: a low-cardinality schema (device-class, row-height, avg-visible-columns, scroll-speed-bucket) with privacy-preserving defaults and opt-out noted in design docs
Scrollbar attenuation visual language: thin state, hover-expand, minimal contrast in default density but meets 4.5:1 contrast on focus/hover for accessibility
Prototype in Figma with three density presets (compact, default, relaxed) showing deferred hydration states and skeleton affordances
Performance baseline: 25% reduction in median main-thread CPU work for sample large table (100k rows x 20 columns) in Chrome on a mid-range device when decorators are deferred
Engineering integration plan with runtime flag and telemetry events documented and handed off to ENG
Accessibility: keyboard focusability remains immediate for interactive affordances; screen reader announces presence of deferred affordance with 'preview available' aria label
design_decisions: Defer non-essential UI hydration instead of lazy-rendering cells to preserve semantic DOM order for accessibility
Use a short idle window (300–700ms) rather than timeouts tied to scroll velocity to avoid unexpected UX when user pauses briefly
Expose a token set for scrollbar thickness and animation-duration so teams can opt into platform-wide motion standards
Density telemetry will be aggregated and stripped of PII; opt-out will be layered into analytics settings
Provide an explicit developer API flag (deferColumnHydration: true) as well as a console-level toggle to experiment with rollout
engineering_notes: ENG asked for a deterministic API: will implement DeferManager that exposes onIdle() hook tied to requestIdleCallback fallback and a cancel on scroll
Potential trade-off: deferring may delay important inline actions; we mark critical affordances as 'eager' via attribute data-eager
Memory impact: by not mounting decorators we expect lower retained DOM nodes and fewer event listeners — measure in canary
Telemetry plan: events to include tableId, columnsHydratedCount, hydrationDelayMs bucketed, deviceClass. No cell content in payloads
Interop with virtualization: must ensure virtualization virtual window size accounts for potential deferred elements to avoid jumpy layout when mounted

2026-03-03 - Noor Patel (ENG Lead): Engineering prototyped DeferManager using requestIdleCallback with scroll cancelation. Observed 28% median CPU reduction in synthetic harness. Need to handle keyboard tabbing edge-case.
2026-03-08 - Accessibility review by Priya Shah: Screen reader flow acceptable if aria-live used to announce deferred interactivity. Ensure focusable controls are not removed from DOM when deferred.
